## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

#d

```{r}
# Calculate the overall and seasonal averages

# 1. season
season_means <- hw1data %>%
  group_by(Season) %>%
  summarise(across(c(PH, IFP, NLP, NGP, NGL, NS, MHG, GY), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(Season = as.character(Season))

# 2. overall
overall_means <- hw1data %>%
  summarise(across(c(PH, IFP, NLP, NGP, NGL, NS, MHG, GY), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(Season = "Overall")

# 3. combine
bind_rows(season_means, overall_means)

```

```{r}
t.test(GY ~ Season, data = hw1data)

```

#c

```{r}
adult[adult == " ?"] <- NA

missing_count
```

#d

```{r}
n_before <- nrow(adult)
n_before

# working 10 hours per week
adult1 <- adult[adult$hours_per_week >= 10, ]

# sample after 
n_after <- nrow(adult1)
n_after
```

#e

```{r}
adult2 <- adult1[!is.na(adult1$occupation) & !is.na(adult1$workclass) & !is.na(adult1$native_country), ]

# comfirm sample
nrow(adult2)

#Occupation, workclass, and native_comountry are categorical variables, and missing values cannot be reasonably filled with means or medians.

#Deleting can avoid errors or deviations caused by missing values during modeling.
```

#f

```{r}
# Eliminate any observations with: age less than 18, age greater than 90
adult3 <- adult2[adult2$age >= 18 & adult2$age <= 90, ]

# Eliminate any observations with education level identified as Preschool.
adult4 <- adult3[adult3$education != "Preschool", ]
```

#g

```{r}
#final sample
n_final <- nrow(adult4)
n_final
```

#Q3 #a

```{r}
nextHappy <- function(n){
  if(!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1 || is.na(n)){
    stop("Input must be a single numeric value.")
  }
  if(n != as.integer(n)){
    stop("Input must be an integer.")
  }
  if(n <= 0){
    stop("Input must be a positive integer.")
  }
  
  digits <- as.integer(strsplit(as.character(n), "")[[1]])
  
  return(sum(digits^2))
}
nextHappy(19)   # 1^2 + 9^2 = 1 + 81 = 82
nextHappy(82)   # 8^2 + 2^2 = 64 + 4 = 68
```

#b

```{r}
happySequence <- function(n) {
  # input
  if (!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1 || is.na(n)) {
    stop("Input must be a single numeric value.")
  }
  if (n != as.integer(n)) {
    stop("Input must be an integer.")
  }
  if (n <= 0) {
    stop("Input must be a positive integer.")
  }
  
  seq_vals <- c(n)   # store
  seen <- c(n)       # test circle
  
  if (n == 1) {
    return(list(sequence = 1, isHappy = TRUE))
  }
  
  repeat {
    next_val <- nextHappy(seq_vals[length(seq_vals)])
    seq_vals <- c(seq_vals, next_val)
    
    if (next_val == 1) {
      return(list(sequence = seq_vals, isHappy = TRUE))
    }
    
    # circle
    if (next_val %in% seen) {
      return(list(sequence = seq_vals, isHappy = FALSE))
    }
    
    seen <- c(seen, next_val)
  }
}

happySequence(19)
happySequence(4)
```

#c. Among integers 1 through 1000:

```{r}
results <- sapply(1:1000, function(x) happySequence(x)$isHappy)
seq_info <- lapply(1:1000, function(x) happySequence(x))
# How many are happy?
num_happy <- sum(results)
cat("happy numbers between 1 and 1000 is", num_happy, "\n")

# What percentage are happy?
pct_happy <- mean(results) * 100
cat("Percentage of happy numbers is", round(pct_happy, 2), "%\n")

# What starting value produces the longest happy sequence before terminating?
seq_lengths <- sapply(seq_info, function(x) {
  if (x$isHappy) {
    return(length(x$sequence))
  } else {
    return(NA)  # unhappy number 不参与排名
  }
})

max_length <- max(seq_lengths, na.rm = TRUE)
start_with_max <- which(seq_lengths == max_length)

cat("Maximum happy sequence length before terminating:", max_length, "\n")
cat("Starting value(s) with the longest happy sequence:", start_with_max, "\n")
```
